description: Render engines the visual director can route a scene to, the signals that route it, the pinned engine builds, and the engines evaluated and turned down. Read by scripts/visual-director.py and the visual-director skill. Evaluation and evidence: docs/visual-engines.md.

hyperframes.name: HyperFrames + GSAP 3 + studio runtime
hyperframes.role: The compositor and the default engine. Every film is a HyperFrames composition; other engines only supply plates to it.
best_for: kinetic typography, captions, titles, labels, numbers
math visuals drawn as SVG (axes, curves, geometry, vectors)
per-format layouts (portrait, landscape, square) from one source
hyperframes.cost: low: one headless Chrome, about 0.4 GB peak, about 1.5 s per film second at 720p

threejs.name: Three.js r158 inside the HyperFrames page
threejs.role: Real-time stylised 3D that must stay a pure function of film time and carry HTML labels that track 3D anchors.
best_for: stylised or toon 3D objects and characters (the 3D Tibi)
turntables and orbits of simple models with tracked labels
3D charts, globes, molecules and lattices with flat or toon shading
anything that must change when the composition changes, with no pre-render step
threejs.cost: low to medium: same browser, software or hardware WebGL; no global illumination

blender.name: Blender (headless, Python bpy) rendering plates
blender.role: Offline 3D plates (opaque MP4 or alpha WebM) that HyperFrames composites under or over its DOM layers. Never carries text.
best_for: physically based light: glass, refraction, caustics, subsurface, soft shadows, global illumination
volumetrics: fog, god rays, smoke, fire, clouds
simulations: rigid bodies, cloth, fluids, particles with lighting
cinematic cameras: real depth of field, motion blur, long dolly and crane moves through 3D environments
3D environments and landscapes, product hero shots, planets and terrain
blender.cost: high: a second toolchain; EEVEE seconds per frame, Cycles tens of seconds per frame on the M2; one heavy job at a time

routing.description: Signals are matched case-insensitively against a storyboard scene's title, visual, layout, beats, capabilities and asset_refs. `terms` name a visual treatment and always count; `subject_terms` name what is shown and count only when no 2D form term (the compositor's `terms`: chart, diagram, equation, ...) is present, because a chart about water is still a chart. The engine with the highest weighted score wins; a tie or a score under min_score stays on the cheaper engine. A heuristic draft only: the visual director decides.

composition_modes.native: Drawn entirely in the HyperFrames page (SVG, DOM, Canvas, or Three.js).
composition_modes.plate-full: An opaque Blender plate fills the frame; HyperFrames adds text and graphics above it.
composition_modes.plate-under: An opaque or alpha plate sits behind HyperFrames graphics as an environment or backdrop.
composition_modes.plate-over: An alpha plate (VP9 WebM) sits above some DOM layers and below the text: an object, particles or fog in front of a diagram.

blender.license: GPL-2.0-or-later (the application); renders are the author's own work

remotion.reason: A second headless-Chromium frame renderer that duplicates HyperFrames (React components instead of a GSAP timeline), with a Webpack build and multi-process rendering measured above 2 GB on the 8 GB host. Source-available licence, not OSI: free for individuals and for-profit organisations of up to 3 employees, a company licence above that.

revideo.reason: A Motion Canvas fork (TSX generator functions, Vite build) that duplicates what HyperFrames + GSAP + SVG already render; rejected in specs/motion-graphics-evolution-report.md section 5.2; upstream activity has slowed since its lead contributor left in 2025.

manim.reason: Manim Community (MIT, Python) is the strongest code-driven engine for equation morphing and LaTeX-heavy math. Not installed: it needs a LaTeX distribution (gigabytes) and a third plate pipeline. Revisit when a brief needs equation-to-equation transforms that SVG + GSAP cannot carry.
